item.title: Tagging?
item.content:encoded:
Should this be tagged goi-format instead of tale? From the Tags Guide, goi-format is defined as:

Anomaly or SCP has been written up from the perspective of a specific Group of Interest, and conforms to the format(s) laid out in that GoI's hub page.

In this case, it fulfils both prerequisites (written from ORIA's POV and adhering to format as stated in the established ORIA GoI hub).

Part of the issue is that neither the Foundation nor ORIA are necessarily inclined towards any greater degree of honest than is necessary. The major issue is that with the Foundation, there's always the implied barrier between "this is the thing that you, having X authorization level, may know" versus "this is the thing that you may not know" versus "this is the thing that we want you to think, whether it's accurate or not, for whatever nebulous motives we have". With ORIA, the contrast is between "this is the thing I am telling you" versus "this is the thing that I casually assume that you already know, so I will make oblique references to it without elaborating". It's part of why the ORIA format allows for so much information to be implied without stating a thing.

Cain is, here, implied to be Ahriman or an agent thereof. It's unclear whether he is manipulating the Foundation, vice versa, or both at once. Cain is, therefore, associated in some way with the Daevas, while Zoroaster!Able is aligned against them and wishes to counter their influence. The secondary implication is that Cain is enabling the Foundation to assist the Daevas, whether the Foundation knows it or not. This is separate from Djoric's labarinthine canon for the Daevas, which I can't even process all of enough to fit into this canon. (I also haven't planned out what role the Daevas actually play in this world as yet.)

After a few runs of re-reading this article, I want to express some of my headcanon w.r.t this article.

+ show block
– hide block

I have noted that many aspects attributed to Zoroaster!Able are vastly different from the canon Able (revival ability works differently etc.). It appears that the Foundation is hiding information about Zoroaster!Able, including his true nature… which is suspicious. And then, we also have to consider Ahriman!Cain, who is compared to Ahriman (or Angra Mainyu) in some of his abilities.

My headcanon is that Ahriman!Cain somehow managed to manipulate the O5 and entrap Zoroaster!Able for his objectives. Documentation has been altered such that everyone would assume Zoroaster!Able is a violent maniac. If we use the multiple clearance style in SCP-2317, I could see Level 2-4 documents on Zoroaster!Able to reference it as a dangerous murderous machine. The Level 5 document would explain its true nature and the reason why they must fake the entire documentation (to imprison Zoroaster!Able and keep him away from… the rise of the Daevas maybe?).

While there is the ORIA politics and djinni we all know and love, this article presents a rather serious implication of a Foundation compromised by anomalies.

But all that above could just be another guy's BS.

I was going to upvote before reading the spoilers. The level of research and Eskobar's view of ORIA as an organisation and a secret society with its own cultural sub-currents makes this a breathing, living piece of writing. I think this is what Kate McTiriss once said it was needed in this wiki, documentation written in such a way that IMPLIES lots of things going on in the background, because the author has actually put a lot of thought about them without writing them verbatim in the document itself.

In fewer words, yes please feed me more Zoroastrian + djinni + muddy internal politics ORIA.

+1

item.content:encoded:
SPOILERS
Hide

Starring Able in the role of "literally fucking Zoroaster."

I always liked Cain more than Able, so I wanted to do something that increased the similarities between them, making them sort of a dualistic, almost Gnostic sort of power-demigod-immortal pairing, and especially wanted to depict how Able would be seen as the "good guy" to Cain's "bad guy" (if you want to apply those sorts of analyses in the first place). And I wanted to do an ORIA thing, and since my headcanon of ORIA includes a lot of ancient Middle Eastern paganism, Gnosticism, and themes of duality and reality, it all sort of meshed together. So in essence, I took Cain's document, inverted a lot of the characteristics (plant death --> increased fertility, perfect memory -—> forgetfulness, etc.), applied Able's appearance, and made some…modifications to increase the (already surprisingly present) Zoroastrian themes that were going on, and that are just as Iranian as Islam is. And here it is.

The ORIA canon that I put together for the GOI contest last year very much incorporates the idea that ORIA, as an organization, is connected to the protection of Iran and the Middle Eastern region as a whole from outside influences, rather than being necessarily tied to Islam or the government of the Islamic Republic of Iran (which ORIA predates by decades) as such (the name of the organization notwithstanding). The two often go hand in hand, but not always. I would imagine there are several factions in ORIA that would absolutely shit themselves if they were privy to these plans, and the government of Iran would obviously attempt a crackdown immediately if this became wider knowledge, for both the religious and the political objections.
